_comment: Batch 01 (Set 1). Distractor-only rewrites to remove the longest-answer cue. Correct options and rationales are unchanged; each distractor keeps its original meaning and stays wrong for the same reason.

RN-S01-01.A: A client with new-onset atrial fibrillation on a diltiazem infusion whose heart rate has decreased from 142/min to 88/min, with BP 118/72 mm Hg
RN-S01-01.C: A client with chronic heart failure, on 2 L/min oxygen with SpO2 95%, who is requesting acetaminophen for chronic knee pain rated 4/10
RN-S01-01.D: A client with stable angina who is NPO for a stress test scheduled in 2 hours and is asking for a drink of water because of a dry, uncomfortable mouth

RN-S01-02.A: Increase the infusion rate as directed by the protocol and recheck the aPTT 6 hours after the rate change
RN-S01-02.C: Administer protamine sulfate IV push now to reverse the heparin, then notify the provider of the result
RN-S01-02.D: Continue the infusion at the current rate and recheck the aPTT in 6 hours as the protocol schedules

RN-S01-06.A: Mediastinal chest tube drainage of 90 mL in the past hour, which is serosanguineous and slightly less than the previous hour's total of 100 mL, with stable vital signs
RN-S01-06.B: Temperature of 99.5°F (37.5°C), with warm, dry skin and the client shivering slightly after rewarming in the intensive care unit
RN-S01-06.D: Incisional pain rated 6 on a 0–10 scale, with the client splinting the sternum when coughing and asking for the next scheduled dose of prescribed IV analgesic

RN-S01-10.A: Deli turkey sandwich on white bread with mustard, a dill pickle spear, and a small bag of potato chips
RN-S01-10.C: Canned chicken noodle soup with a side of saltine crackers and a glass of tomato juice
RN-S01-10.D: Frozen macaroni and cheese dinner with a side of canned green beans and a diet soda

RN-S01-11.B: "Report any flushing or warmth of your face and neck after taking the dose."
RN-S01-11.C: "Report if your stools become dark green or change color after a week."
RN-S01-11.D: "Report any increase in appetite or weight gain over the first month."

RN-S01-14.A: Palpate the abdomen to assess the size and tenderness of the pulsating mass before notifying the provider
RN-S01-14.B: Administer the prescribed PRN oral analgesic for the back pain and reassess the pain level in 30 minutes
RN-S01-14.D: Place the client in a prone position to relieve the back pain and pressure on the aneurysm

RN-S01-17.A: Reduce the BP to 120/80 mm Hg as quickly as possible to protect the brain and kidneys
RN-S01-17.C: Maintain the current BP without titrating the infusion until a head CT scan is completed
RN-S01-17.D: Reduce the systolic BP to below 100 mm Hg within the first hour of the infusion

RN-S01-24.A: Administer the prescribed IV furosemide and begin measuring hourly urine output
RN-S01-24.C: Reinforce teaching about a 2-g sodium diet and limiting fluids at home
RN-S01-24.D: Obtain the client's weight on a standing scale to compare with the dry weight

PN-S01-01.B: A client admitted 30 minutes ago reporting new chest pain that started at rest this morning
PN-S01-01.C: A client receiving a nitroglycerin infusion being titrated every 5 minutes to chest pain
PN-S01-01.D: A client with a new diagnosis of heart failure who needs an initial assessment and teaching plan

PN-S01-04.A: Administer the digoxin as scheduled and recheck the apical pulse in 30 minutes
PN-S01-04.C: Recount the pulse radially and administer the digoxin if it is above 60/min
PN-S01-04.D: Administer the digoxin with a full glass of water and document the pulse rate

PN-S01-06.A: "I'll sit down before I take a tablet, in case it makes me feel lightheaded or dizzy."
PN-S01-06.B: "If my pain isn't better 5 minutes after the first tablet, I'll call 911 right away."
PN-S01-06.D: "I may get a headache after taking it, and that usually means the medicine is working."

PN-S01-07.B: White rice, white bread, and pasta
PN-S01-07.C: Cheese, whole milk, and plain yogurt

PN-S01-08.A: "Take the medication only on days when you have a headache or feel flushed."
PN-S01-08.C: "Increase your salt intake if you feel dizzy or lightheaded during the day."
PN-S01-08.D: "Stop the medication if you feel more tired than usual for a few days."

PN-S01-09.A: Expel the air bubble from the prefilled syringe before injecting the medication
PN-S01-09.C: Massage the injection site for 1 minute afterward to improve absorption
PN-S01-09.D: Aspirate for blood before injecting to confirm the needle isn't in a vessel

PN-S01-11.A: "You may raise the head of the bed and sit fully upright to eat now, as long as you keep your right leg straight."
PN-S01-11.C: "You can bend your right knee to get comfortable while you eat, as long as you move it slowly, gently, and carefully."
PN-S01-11.D: "You may get up and walk to the chair to eat once the nurse removes the pressure dressing from your right groin."

PN-S01-14.A: "I'll use a heating pad on my feet at night when they feel cold."
PN-S01-14.C: "I'll elevate my legs above my heart when they start to hurt."
PN-S01-14.D: "I'll wear snug, tight socks to keep my feet warm at night."

PN-S01-15.A: "Keep your legs dangling over the side of the bed as much as possible."
PN-S01-15.C: "Avoid walking and stay off your feet to protect the ulcer while it heals."
PN-S01-15.D: "Sit with your legs crossed at the knee to improve circulation to the ulcer."

PN-S01-16.A: After the client has been up and walking for about an hour
PN-S01-16.C: At bedtime, just before the client goes to sleep
PN-S01-16.D: After the evening shower, once the skin is dry

PN-S01-17.A: "I'll weigh myself whenever my ankles or feet look more swollen than usual."
PN-S01-17.C: "I'll call my provider if I gain 5 pounds or more over the course of a month."
PN-S01-17.D: "I'll weigh myself once a week, wearing my coat and shoes, on whichever scale is closest."

PN-S01-18.A: A small bag of salted pretzels with cheese dip
PN-S01-18.C: A cup of canned tomato soup with crackers
PN-S01-18.D: A hot dog on a bun with mustard and relish

PN-S01-20.A: "You shouldn't worry about that right now. Focus on getting better first."
PN-S01-20.C: "That's a question you'll need to ask your cardiologist about at your next follow-up visit."
PN-S01-20.D: "Sexual activity is not safe for several months after a heart attack."

PN-S01-23.A: Trace ankle edema at the end of the day that is gone by morning
PN-S01-23.C: Fatigue after walking to the dining room that improves with rest
PN-S01-23.D: Nocturia twice nightly, which is the resident's usual pattern
